# Jira vs Plane (2026)

## Overview
Jira and Plane are two popular project management tools used by software development teams and other organizations to track and manage their work. This comparison is beneficial for teams considering switching from Jira to Plane, possibly due to the core use case of issue tracking and project management, and the key reason being the desire for more control over their data and costs. The main difference between the two tools is their approach to data ownership and cost structure.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Jira is a paid tool with a per-user monthly fee, while Plane is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: Plane allows users to have full control over their data, while Jira stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Jira has a more complex setup process, while Plane is relatively easier to set up.
* Scalability: Jira is more scalable and can handle larger teams and projects, while Plane is better suited for smaller to medium-sized teams.
* Integration: Jira has a wider range of integrations with other tools and services, while Plane has a more limited set of integrations, but includes a native integration with Git.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Jira | Plane |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $7.75-$14.50/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $387.50-$725/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,550-$2,900/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Jira:**
* Wide range of integrations with other tools and services
* Scalable and can handle large teams and projects
* Robust set of features for project management and issue tracking
* Well-established and widely used in the industry
* Good customer support
**Plane:**
* Free and self-hosted, giving users full control over their data
* Easy to set up and use
* Native integration with Git
* Customizable and flexible
* Limited costs, only requiring server maintenance

## When to Choose Each
Jira is a good choice for large teams and organizations that require a robust set of features for project management and issue tracking, and are willing to pay for the service. It is also a good choice for teams that are already invested in the Atlassian ecosystem and want to take advantage of the integrations with other tools and services. Plane, on the other hand, is a good choice for smaller to medium-sized teams that want more control over their data and costs, and are looking for a free and self-hosted solution. It is also a good choice for teams that are looking for a simple and easy-to-use tool for issue tracking and project management.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from Jira in CSV or JSON format.
2. Set up a Plane server and configure it to your needs.
3. Use the Plane import tool to import your data from the CSV or JSON file.
4. Configure any additional settings or integrations as needed.
5. Test the migration to ensure that all data has been transferred correctly.

## Our Take
Plane is not yet production-ready for most users, as it is still a relatively new tool and lacks some of the features and integrations that Jira has. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is that Plane does not yet have a built-in reporting feature, which may be a deal-breaker for some teams. However, for teams that are looking for a free and self-hosted solution and are willing to put in the time and effort to set it up and customize it, Plane may be a good choice.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams of less than 10 users that do not need advanced project management features
* Teams that are looking for a free and self-hosted solution and are willing to put in the time and effort to set it up and customize it
* Teams that are already using Git and want a native integration with their issue tracking tool
* Teams that are looking for a simple and easy-to-use tool for issue tracking and project management
* Teams that are on a tight budget and cannot afford the costs of Jira

## FAQ
### Can I use Plane for large teams?
No, Plane is currently better suited for smaller to medium-sized teams.
### Is Plane free?
Yes, Plane is free and self-hosted.
### Can I integrate Plane with other tools and services?
Yes, Plane has a limited set of integrations, but it is customizable and can be integrated with other tools and services using APIs.
### How do I migrate my data from Jira to Plane?
You can export your data from Jira in CSV or JSON format and then use the Plane import tool to import it.
### Is Plane production-ready?
Not yet, Plane is still a relatively new tool and lacks some of the features and integrations that Jira has.

title: Trello vs WeKan

# Trello vs WeKan (2026)

## Overview
Trello and WeKan are project management tools that help teams organize and track their work. This comparison is useful for teams looking to switch from a proprietary, cloud-based solution like Trello to a self-hosted, open-source alternative like WeKan. The core use case for both tools is task and project management, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Trello offers a free plan and several paid plans, while WeKan is free and open-source, with costs limited to self-hosting.
* Data ownership: WeKan allows teams to host their own data, while Trello stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: WeKan requires more technical expertise to set up and configure, while Trello is generally easier to get started with.
* Scalability: Trello is designed to scale with large teams and enterprises, while WeKan may require more customization and configuration to support large-scale deployments.
* Integration with Google Drive: Trello has a native integration with Google Drive, while WeKan relies on third-party plugins and integrations.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Trello | WeKan |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $5+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $250/month (Standard plan) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $1,000/month (Premium plan) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Trello:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Robust integration with other tools and services
* Scalable and reliable
* Mobile apps available
* Limited control over data and customization
**WeKan:**
* Free and open-source
* Self-hosting available for data control
* Customizable and extensible
* Community-driven development
* Steeper learning curve and more technical expertise required

## When to Choose Each
Trello is a good choice for teams that prioritize ease of use and scalability, and are willing to pay for a proprietary solution. It's ideal for large teams and enterprises that need a reliable and robust project management tool. WeKan, on the other hand, is a good choice for teams that value data control and customization, and are willing to invest time and technical expertise into setting up and configuring the tool. It's ideal for small to medium-sized teams and organizations that prioritize openness and community-driven development.

## Migration Path
1. Export Trello boards and data in JSON format using the Trello API or a third-party tool.
2. Set up a WeKan instance on a self-hosted server or a cloud provider.
3. Use the WeKan import tool to import the exported Trello data into WeKan.
4. Configure and customize WeKan to fit the team's needs and workflow.
5. Test and verify that all data and functionality have been successfully migrated.

## Our Take
WeKan is not yet production-ready for most users, as it still lacks some of the polish and features of Trello. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that WeKan's integration with third-party tools and services is still limited and may require custom development. However, for teams that value data control and customization, and are willing to invest time and technical expertise, WeKan is a viable alternative to Trello. We recommend switching to WeKan for teams that are already familiar with open-source tools and have the technical expertise to set up and configure the platform.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) that prioritize data control and customization
* Teams that are already using open-source tools and have the technical expertise to set up and configure WeKan
* Organizations that value community-driven development and are willing to contribute to the WeKan project
* Teams that do not need native integration with Google Drive or other proprietary services
* Teams that are looking for a free and self-hosted alternative to Trello

## FAQ
### Can I migrate my Trello data to WeKan?
Yes, you can export your Trello data in JSON format and import it into WeKan using the WeKan import tool.
### Is WeKan free?
Yes, WeKan is free and open-source, with costs limited to self-hosting.
### Does WeKan have a mobile app?
No, WeKan does not have a native mobile app, but it can be accessed through a web browser on mobile devices.
### Can I integrate WeKan with Google Drive?
Not natively, but WeKan relies on third-party plugins and integrations to integrate with Google Drive and other services.
### Is WeKan scalable?
WeKan can be scaled to support large teams and enterprises, but may require more customization and configuration than Trello.

title: Dropbox vs Nextcloud
comparison_markdown:
# Dropbox vs Nextcloud

## Overview

Dropbox is one of the original cloud storage services offering simple file sync. Nextcloud is the most popular self-hosted cloud platform combining file storage, calendar, contacts, video calls, and 400+ apps.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Dropbox charges $9.99-$16.58/user/month; Nextcloud is free to self-host
- **Storage**: Nextcloud storage is limited only by your server disk space
- **Feature breadth**: Nextcloud is far more than storage; it is a full Google Workspace alternative
- **Privacy**: Nextcloud on your own server means only you can access your data
- **Setup**: Dropbox is instant; Nextcloud requires Docker setup

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Dropbox | Nextcloud |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $9.99-$16.58/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$500/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$1,998/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Dropbox

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Nextcloud

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [nextcloud/server](https://github.com/nextcloud/server) * ~27k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Dropbox if:** Dropbox suits individuals or small teams wanting simple reliable file sync with no infrastructure to manage.

**Choose Nextcloud if:** Nextcloud suits privacy-focused organizations wanting to eliminate cloud subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Download all Dropbox files locally, then upload to Nextcloud via the web interface or desktop sync client.

## Our Take

Nextcloud is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Dropbox tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Nextcloud instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Dropbox, switching to self-hosted Nextcloud will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Dropbox until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Dropbox paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Nextcloud free to use?
Yes. Nextcloud is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Dropbox to Nextcloud?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Dropbox data, follow the Nextcloud import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Nextcloud get regular updates?
Yes. Nextcloud has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Nextcloud without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Nextcloud development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Dropbox](https://dropbox.com) and [Nextcloud](https://nextcloud.com) before making decisions.*
meta_description: Nextcloud is a free, self-hosted alternative to Dropbox. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.

# Zoom vs Jitsi Meet (2026)

Zoom and Jitsi Meet are video conferencing tools that enable teams to collaborate remotely. This comparison is beneficial for teams seeking to switch from a proprietary platform to a self-hosted solution, with a core use case of secure and customizable video meetings. * Cost: Zoom offers a free plan with limitations, while Jitsi Meet is completely free and open-source.

* Setup complexity: Jitsi Meet requires more technical expertise to set up, especially for self-hosting, compared to Zoom's user-friendly interface.
* Scalability: Zoom is designed for large-scale enterprises and can handle thousands of users, while Jitsi Meet is better suited for smaller to medium-sized teams.
* Feature difference: Zoom offers more advanced features like virtual whiteboards and polling, whereas Jitsi Meet has a more straightforward and minimalist approach to video conferencing.

| Aspect | Zoom | Jitsi Meet |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $13.33+/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |

**Zoom:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Advanced features like virtual whiteboards and polling
* Large user base and community support
* Scalable for large enterprises
* Integrates with many third-party tools
* Limited control over data and security
* Costly for large teams

* Self-hosting option for full control over data

4. Configure your Jitsi Meet instance to match your team's requirements, including security and customization settings.

Jitsi Meet is not yet production-ready for most users due to its complexity and limited user support. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Jitsi Meet requires a significant amount of technical expertise to set up and maintain, especially for self-hosting. However, for teams that value security, customization, and cost-effectiveness, Jitsi Meet is a great option, and we recommend switching from Zoom to Jitsi Meet if you have a small to medium-sized team with technical expertise and don't require advanced features.

* Small teams (less than 10 users) that don't need advanced features like virtual whiteboards

* Teams with technical expertise that can handle setup and maintenance
* Teams that require self-hosting for compliance or regulatory reasons
* Non-profit organizations or educational institutions that need a free and open-source solution

## FAQ

### Can I self-host Jitsi Meet?

No, Jitsi Meet is considered more secure than Zoom due to its self-hosting option and open-source nature.
### Can I integrate Jitsi Meet with other tools?
Yes, Jitsi Meet has an API that allows integration with other tools and platforms.
### Is Jitsi Meet suitable for large enterprises?
No, Jitsi Meet is not suitable for very large teams due to its limited scalability and lack of advanced features.

# Microsoft Teams vs Mattermost (2026)

## Overview
Microsoft Teams and Mattermost are two popular communication and collaboration platforms designed for teams and businesses. Both tools offer a range of features to facilitate team communication, file sharing, and project management. This comparison is beneficial for teams considering switching from Microsoft Teams to Mattermost, particularly those valuing data ownership and self-hosting capabilities.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Microsoft Teams offers a free plan and paid plans starting at $6 per user/month, while Mattermost is free and open-source with optional self-hosting.
* Data Ownership: Mattermost allows users to retain full ownership of their data, whereas Microsoft Teams stores data on its servers.
* Setup Complexity: Microsoft Teams has a more straightforward setup process, while Mattermost requires more technical expertise for self-hosting.
* Scalability: Both platforms are scalable, but Mattermost's self-hosting option provides more control over scalability.
* Integration: Microsoft Teams has native integration with Microsoft Office tools, while Mattermost offers integration with a range of third-party tools through its open API.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Microsoft Teams | Mattermost |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $6-$22/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | MIT / AGPL |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $6-$22/user/month (approx. $300-$1100/month) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $6-$22/user/month (approx. $1200-$4400/month) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Microsoft Teams:**
* Easy to set up and use
* Native integration with Microsoft Office tools
* Wide range of features and integrations
* Large user community
* Limited control over data ownership
**Mattermost:**
* Self-hosting option for full data ownership
* Customizable and extensible through open API
* Free and open-source
* Community-driven development

# Google Workspace vs Nextcloud

## Overview

Google suite of cloud productivity tools including Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Meet, and Calendar. is a popular proprietary tool in the productivity space. Nextcloud is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Google Workspace costs $6-$18/user/month; Nextcloud is Free (self-hosted)
- **License**: Google Workspace is Proprietary; Nextcloud is AGPL 3.0
- **Data ownership**: Nextcloud can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Nextcloud eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Nextcloud has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Google Workspace | Nextcloud |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $6-$18/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$300/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$1,200/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Google Workspace

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Nextcloud

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [nextcloud/server](https://github.com/nextcloud/server) * ~27k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Google Workspace if:** Google Workspace is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Nextcloud if:** Nextcloud is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Google Workspace in its standard export format, review Nextcloud import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Nextcloud is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Google Workspace tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Nextcloud instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Google Workspace, switching to self-hosted Nextcloud will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Google Workspace until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Google Workspace paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Nextcloud free to use?
Yes. Nextcloud is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Google Workspace to Nextcloud?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Google Workspace data, follow the Nextcloud import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Nextcloud get regular updates?
Yes. Nextcloud has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Nextcloud without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Nextcloud development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Google Workspace](https://workspace.google.com) and [Nextcloud](https://nextcloud.com) before making decisions.*
